reasons: The tests were read but not run during this review.
The file states the negative rules clearly, which is good evidence of intent.

terms.meaning: the most independent a system may be, from fully automated down to human only
a rule, such as a regulation, that limits what a process may do automatically
a link from a finding to the specific process steps it applies to
a set of numeric ratings of a process, set by a different stage
a text pattern used to detect a family of phrases, such as a number out of five

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and purpose of the file
sections.what: Brings in the assessor, error types, schema types, and shared stub and run context. The docstring says the negative tests matter most.
sections.why: Makes clear which tests are the important ones.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Async runner choice
sections.what: Tells the async test runner to use asyncio.
sections.why: Likely reason: the agent code is written for asyncio.

sections.name: current_state
sections.title: Sample current state
sections.what: Builds a sample current state with a chosen number of steps, each with an effort share and a citation.
sections.why: Gives the assessor a process to check constraints against, and lets tests set how many steps exist.
sections.watch_out: Step count controls which anchors are valid, so change it with the anchor tests in mind.

sections.name: constraint
sections.title: Sample constraint
sections.what: Builds a sample regulatory constraint with a chosen autonomy ceiling, requirement text, and affected steps.
sections.why: Provides a realistic constraint to test against, with a default that limits the step to agent with review.

sections.name: readiness
sections.title: Sample data readiness
sections.what: Builds a sample data readiness block with two required datasets, one available and governed, and one gap.
sections.why: Gives a known readiness picture, so the ratio test has a known answer.

sections.name: output
sections.title: Sample assessor output
sections.what: Builds a full assessor answer from the given constraints and gaps, with two citations.
sections.why: The default answer most tests start from.

sections.name: TestHappyPath
sections.title: Normal assessment
sections.what: Checks a valid run returns a feasibility assessment, that the constraint is kept, that the agent uses the standard model tier, that the task text lists every ceiling and constraint kind, and that every step reaches the model.
sections.why: Confirms the normal path and that the model is given the options and steps it needs.
sections.watch_out: A constraint that points at a step the model never saw is a guess, so the step list must reach the prompt.

sections.name: TestTheCeilingIsComputedNotOffered
sections.title: Ceiling is computed, not offered
sections.what: Checks the model's output has no overall ceiling field, the task text says not to state one, the strictest constraint sets the binding ceiling, and no constraints gives full autonomy along with the evidence ids.
sections.why: The overall ceiling is a decision made from all constraints together, so the model must not be asked for it. Empty constraints are a finding of what was checked, so evidence must come with it.
sections.watch_out: Adding an overall ceiling field to the output would defeat this stage's rule.

sections.name: TestItDoesNotScore
sections.title: Scores are refused
sections.what: Checks that the output does not contain scored dimensions, that scores written into constraints or gaps are refused with a message about scoring, and that ordinary prose about data is accepted.
sections.why: Scoring belongs to another stage. The check must catch scores but must not block the normal data descriptions this stage exists to produce.
sections.watch_out: The check is a pattern match, so a too-broad pattern would make the stage unusable and tempt someone to remove the check.

sections.name: TestDanglingAnchors
sections.title: Constraints must point at real steps
sections.what: Checks that a constraint pointing at a missing step is refused, that the retry carries the correction and gets a valid anchor, and that a process-wide constraint with no step anchors is allowed.
sections.why: A link to a step that does not exist is a wrong finding. A process-wide constraint is valid and should not be forced onto a step.

sections.name: TestDataReadiness
sections.title: Data readiness rules
sections.what: Checks that an available dataset not listed as required is refused by the schema, and that the readiness ratio is computed from the returned block, giving one half in the sample.
sections.why: Stops impossible readiness states and makes sure the ratio is calculated, not written by the model.
sections.watch_out: The test's note says the ratio never reaches a process record. Check that note before assuming the number is used downstream.

summary: Tests that the feasibility assessor lists constraints and data gaps, but never scores the process and never picks the overall autonomy ceiling itself.
purpose: Protects two rules: the model cannot set the binding ceiling, and scores cannot sneak into the constraints or gaps text. Everything else is basic arrangement checks.
why: The module description says the two negative tests matter most. The ceiling and scores are decisions that belong to other stages, so this stage must not make them.
how: Builds sample constraints, data readiness, and current state. Then it checks the output schema has no ceiling field, that the strictest constraint binds, that scores written in prose are refused, that step anchors must exist, and that the readiness ratio is computed correctly.
inputs: Sample current state with a chosen number of steps, sample constraints and readiness, and a stub client.
outputs: Pass or fail results. No real model calls.
risks: The score detection uses a pattern match. It must catch scores without blocking normal data prose, and the tests check both sides of that.
debug: If a score is wrongly refused, check the test about ordinary data prose. If a score slips through, check the score patterns in the agent code. For ceiling issues, check the schema fields in the assessor module.
